argument:
The bull's CFO increase to RM62.623m and RM35.491m post-capex cash show genuine operating funding despite RM80.148m receivable absorption. No bank borrowings and liquid assets make the RM118m Taiwan expansion feasible. I accept these strengths rather than treating the entire liquidity pool as unearned.

The shareholder tradeoff remains premium valuation and dilution: RM636.783m warrant proceeds enlarged financing and ownership supply, while other income supported reported profit. At 47.18x trailing and 38.23x forecast earnings, growth must generate larger per-share cash, not merely utilised capacity or higher group earnings. Collections and investment returns can improve, but current cash is modest relative to the headline profit expansion. Constructive volume-backed technicals support interest without cancelling that burden. The bull answers funding feasibility; risk-adjusted entry remains less compelling than business quality.
key_points: Operating CFO and positive FCF are distinct from warrant financing.
Premium valuation, dilution and collections constrain per-share upside.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers that some liquidity is earned and expansion can be funded. It has not resolved the per-share conversion hurdle at 47.18x; financing capacity and profitable utilisation alone do not eliminate dilution and collection costs.
